answer.short:
$x=2+\sqrt6$.

Substitute $u=\sqrt{2x+3}\ge0$ and reject the negative value of $u$.
answer.worked:
Let $u=\sqrt{2x+3}\ge0$. Then $x=u+1$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2&=2(u+1)+3\\u^2-2u-5&=0\\(u-1)^2&=6\\u&=1\pm\sqrt6.\end{align*}$$
Reject $1-\sqrt6<0$. Hence $u=1+\sqrt6$ and $x=2+\sqrt6$.
Check:
$$\begin{align*}(2+\sqrt6)-\sqrt{2(2+\sqrt6)+3}&=2+\sqrt6-\sqrt{(1+\sqrt6)^2}\\(2+\sqrt6)-\sqrt{2(2+\sqrt6)+3}&=1.\end{align*}$$
